SL2.mechanism: A symbol's stable id is built by MonikerBuilder._build (moniker.py:106) as a space-delimited 5-field string 'sutra <language> <repo_name> <file_path> <descriptor>'. Same-name symbols are disambiguated by three composed layers: (1) file_path is a moniker field, so identical names in different files never collide; (2) the descriptor carries a kind suffix appended by the for_* methods — ().  function/method, #  class, .  variable, /  module — plus a scope-chain prefix rendered by _prefix from the enclosing chain (built by the adapter's _scope_chain, python.py:142, which does not stop at function boundaries) so a class vs function, or a nested/function-local vs a top-level def, get distinct descriptors; (3) genuine same-scope same-name collisions are broken by _disambiguate (python.py:471), which keeps the first occurrence and inserts (N) before the trailing suffix for the Nth duplicate, with _dedup_keep_first (indexer.py:64) as a final keep-first backstop.

SS2.mechanism: Repo scope is enforced by physical partitioning, not a query-time filter. The MCP search entrypoint (server.py sutra_search / _unit) selects a per-repo ServingUnit from the SnapshotRegistry via registry.get(repo) (registry.py:82). Each ServingUnit's RetrievalPipeline (and its InMemoryVectorStore/channels) is built from exactly ONE repo's ArtifactSnapshot in build_serving_unit (registry.py:97, snapshot = ArtifactLoader().load(artifact_dir)). RetrievalPipeline.search (pipeline.py:79) takes no repo argument at all — it can only ever see the symbols/vectors of the single snapshot it was constructed from, so a search for repo A physically cannot reach repo B's data. (The vector store's filter_monikers is a within-snapshot kind/candidate filter, NOT repo scoping; sql_reader's `WHERE repo_name=%s` is the incremental-indexing WRITE path and is never on the MCP read path.)
